# Sirach Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_008_page_001.jpg

---

1 Do not quarrel with someone powerful, lest you fall into their hands.

2 Do not dispute with someone rich, lest they outweigh you; for gold has ruined many and has corrupted the minds of kings.

3 Do not strive with a loudmouth, and do not heap wood on their fire.

4 Do not make jokes with an uneducated person, lest your ancestors be disparaged.

5 Do not reproach someone who is turning back from sin; remember that we all deserve punishment.

6 Do not scorn an old person, for some of us will grow old too.

7 Do not rejoice over anyone's death; remember that we all must die.

8 Do not overlook the discourse of the wise; occupy yourself with their sayings, for from them you will learn discipline, and you will know how to stand before great people.

9 Do not ignore the teaching of the elders, for they themselves learned from their parents; from them you will learn discernment and how to give an answer when the time requires it.

10 Do not stoke the fire of a sinner, lest you be burned in his blaze.

11 Do not rise up against the shameless, lest they set a trap for your words.

12 Do not lend to someone more powerful than you — but if you lend anything, consider it as good as lost.

13 Do not stand surety for more than you can afford; and if you do stand surety, be ready to pay.

14 Do not go to law with a judge, for they will rule in their own interest.

15 Do not travel alongside a reckless person, lest they become a burden on you; for they follow only their own impulses, and their foolishness could destroy you along with them.

16 Do not get into a fight with a quick-tempered person, and do not cross the desert with them; for killing means nothing to such a person, and in a deserted place they may cut you down.

17 Do not take a fool into your confidence, for they cannot keep a secret.

18 Do not do anything in private in front of a stranger, for you do not know what they may later spread about.

19 Do not pour out your heart to everyone, and do not expect a return of favors from one who is ungrateful.
